key: That pathway of the Sun in heaven, made to be highly glorified, Is not to be transgressed, O Gods. O mortals, ye behold it not. Mark this my woe, ye Earth and Heaven.
s: In a lament that tells of Trita buried in a well, the singer turns to the Sun’s road; Sāyaṇa, on 1.105.16, reads it as a road even the gods cannot overstep, since the seasons, the sacrifices and so the gods’ life depend on the Sun.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.105.16, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 400930 (2024)

evidence.words: हे देवाः सः अयमादित्यो युष्माभिरपि “न ”अतिक्रमे अतिक्रमितुं न शक्यः । युष्मज्जीवनस्य तदायत्तत्वात् । सति हि सूर्ये वसन्तादयः काला निष्पद्यन्ते । कालेषु च यागाः क्रियन्ते । यागेषु च सत्सु भवतां जीवनम् ।
evidence.gloss: O gods, this Āditya (the Sun) cannot be overstepped even by you, because your life depends on it: for while the Sun is, the seasons, spring and the rest, come about; in the seasons sacrifices are performed; and while there are sacrifices, there is your life.

reason: VERIFIED. Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 1.105.16, at [104,16]). Plain sense faithful: 1.105 is a lament with the refrain to Earth and Heaven, Trita in the well at 1.105.17, the verse addressing the gods about the Sun. Sāyaṇa on 1.105.16 (packet, revision 400930) takes the Āditya, glossed as the path (the ever-going one, or the way of worshippers to Brahma’s world), as not to be overstepped even by the gods, because their life depends on it: the Sun brings the seasons, the seasons the sacrifices, the sacrifices the gods’ life. The sentence carries exactly that chain; Wilson’s note c and Griffith’s note on 16 report the same. entry-check ok.
